text: Lesson 11 already built a Job the simple way — one notebook, one schedule. Here's everything a real production Job supports beyond that single-task case.
This is a real screenshot of the Databricks Jobs UI: one job, four tasks, one daily trigger. Every piece on this screen is a real, configurable part of the Job object.
Lesson 11 only needed a simple schedule. A Job's trigger can also be file arrival, continuous, or manual — file arrival starting a run the moment new data actually lands.
Two job-level settings Lesson 11 didn't need: a retry policy controlling how failures are retried, and a timeout capping how long a run is allowed to take.
A Job is genuinely more than one notebook on a timer. Next up: the Workflows UI, where these tasks actually get built.
